name: ssd-bench-prose-perf-analysis
notes: Long-form prose: performance analysis request with rich numeric data. Token stream is dense with numbers and technical terms. ~660 prompt tokens.

messages.content:
I am benchmarking the KV-cache SSD spill-and-hydrate tier of an MLX inference server on Apple Silicon M4 Max (128 GB unified memory). I have collected the following performance data across three workloads and three NVMe drives. Please analyze the data, identify the bottlenecks, and recommend configuration changes.

Workload A (long-context prefill, 32k token prompts, batch_size=1):
  Drive: Samsung 990 Pro 2 TB (sequential read: 7,450 MB/s, sequential write: 6,900 MB/s)
  Spill events: 240 | Mean spill duration: 48.3 ms | P99 spill: 92.1 ms | Mean spill bytes: 18.4 MB
  Hydrate events: 67 | Mean hydrate duration: 31.7 ms | P99 hydrate: 68.4 ms | Mean hydrate bytes: 18.4 MB
  Computed spill throughput: 18.4 MB / 0.0483 s = 381 MB/s
  Computed hydrate throughput: 18.4 MB / 0.0317 s = 580 MB/s
  Decode TPS with SSD tier enabled: 47.2 | Decode TPS without SSD tier: 49.8
  SSD bytes used: 4.1 GB | Evictions: 0

Workload B (mixed-length prompts, 2k–8k tokens, batch_size=1, high reuse):
  Drive: Samsung 990 Pro 2 TB (same as above)
  Spill events: 1,840 | Mean spill duration: 12.1 ms | P99 spill: 31.4 ms | Mean spill bytes: 3.2 MB
  Hydrate events: 1,102 | Mean hydrate duration: 8.4 ms | P99 hydrate: 24.7 ms | Mean hydrate bytes: 3.2 MB
  Computed spill throughput: 3.2 MB / 0.0121 s = 264 MB/s
  Computed hydrate throughput: 3.2 MB / 0.0084 s = 381 MB/s
  Decode TPS with SSD tier enabled: 61.3 | Decode TPS without SSD tier: 58.9
  SSD bytes used: 5.8 GB | Evictions: 234
  Prompt cache SSD hit rate: 59.9% (1102 / 1840)

Workload C (high-frequency short prompts, 512–1024 tokens, batch_size=1, low reuse):
  Drive: Samsung 990 Pro 2 TB (same as above)
  Spill events: 8,120 | Mean spill duration: 3.9 ms | P99 spill: 11.2 ms | Mean spill bytes: 0.7 MB
  Hydrate events: 41 | Mean hydrate duration: 5.1 ms | P99 hydrate: 18.3 ms | Mean hydrate bytes: 0.7 MB
  Computed spill throughput: 0.7 MB / 0.0039 s = 179 MB/s
  Computed hydrate throughput: 0.7 MB / 0.0051 s = 137 MB/s
  Decode TPS with SSD tier enabled: 84.1 | Decode TPS without SSD tier: 91.7
  SSD bytes used: 5.2 GB | Evictions: 6,847
  Prompt cache SSD hit rate: 0.5% (41 / 8120)

Comparison run on Apple internal SSD (read: 3,500 MB/s, write: 4,500 MB/s) for Workload B:
  Mean hydrate duration: 14.7 ms | Hydrate throughput: 3.2 MB / 0.0147 s = 218 MB/s

Additional context:
  Block size: 256 tokens per block. Each block serialized as a safetensors file.
  Serialization adds ~2.1 ms of CPU overhead per spill event regardless of block size.
  Deserialization adds ~1.8 ms of CPU overhead per hydrate event.
  The SQLite index lookup (dur_lookup_us) averages 0.4 ms per hydrate.
  prompt_cache_slots=8 in all three workloads (RAM tier holds 8 recent sessions).

Based on this data: (1) Identify the dominant bottleneck for each workload. (2) Explain why Workload C is a net-negative use of the SSD tier. (3) Suggest three concrete parameter changes that would improve the net TPS delta for Workload B on the Apple internal SSD. (4) Propose a heuristic that the server could apply automatically to decide whether the SSD tier is beneficial for a given workload, based on observable metrics available at runtime.
